brief: Treasury's November 4 refunding statement deleted "at least" from guidance used since 2024, which said coupon and FRN auction sizes would stay unchanged "for at least the next several quarters." Removing the floor opens the door to long-end auction changes starting in 2027. Headline sizes were unchanged for an 11th straight quarter ($125bn total), and the 7-year note converts to quarterly issuance from March 2027, freeing flexibility in the belly. Citi had forecast $3bn cuts to 20s and 30s, which did not happen. Goldman's Marshall team correctly predicted the softened, two-sided language instead. TBAC recommended unchanged sizes now but said increases are likely warranted in the second half of FY27, concentrated in the 2-to-10-year sector, with "considerable debate" on whether 20s and 30s eventually shrink. The underlying driver: a projected $2.14 trillion FY28-29 funding shortfall is being plugged with bills, pushing the bill share of debt toward 28% by 2029 even as Fed SOMA bill-buying slows, which TBAC flags as a risk to bill-market demand and repo stability.
